slides.title: 6 things to check when you enter your room
slides.sub: Two minutes now saves a bad night later.

slides.title: Is it the room you booked?
slides.body: Bed type, view, number of guests. Easier to fix now than at midnight.

slides.title: Test the heating or air con.
slides.body: Switch it on straight away. If it doesn't work, ask before you unpack.

slides.title: Check the safe.
slides.body: Make sure it opens, locks and opens again before your passport goes in.

slides.title: Take photos of any damage.
slides.body: A stain or a broken lamp? Snap it and tell reception, so nobody blames you later.

slides.title: Find the fire exit.
slides.body: Count the doors to the nearest exit. It takes ten seconds.

slides.title: Ask about late check-out early.
slides.body: Requests made on arrival are often easier for the hotel to plan for.

slides.title: Something wrong with your booking?
slides.body: Our support team answers 7 days a week.

caption:
The first two minutes in a hotel room decide how the rest of the stay goes.

Check the room matches your booking, test the heating or air con, try the safe, photograph any damage, find the fire exit and ask about late check-out early.

slides.title: Paris: where to stay, by vibe
slides.body: 5 neighbourhoods, 5 very different trips.

slides.title: Le Marais
slides.body: Central and walkable. Old mansions, galleries, falafel and the Place des Vosges.

slides.title: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
slides.body: Literary cafés, bookshops and the Luxembourg Gardens nearby.

slides.title: Montmartre
slides.body: Hilltop lanes, Sacré-Cœur and views over the city. Lots of stairs.

slides.title: Latin Quarter
slides.body: Busy streets, small bistros and the Panthéon, close to Notre-Dame.

slides.title: Canal Saint-Martin
slides.body: Iron footbridges, canal-side bars and independent shops.

slides.title: Sleep better in any hotel room
slides.sub: 5 small tricks for a quieter night.

slides.title: Ask for a quiet room when you book.
slides.body: Use the special requests box: high floor, away from the lift and the street.

slides.title: Pack earplugs and an eye mask.
slides.body: They weigh nothing and fix thin walls and curtains that let the light in.

slides.title: Set the temperature early.
slides.body: Most people sleep better in a cool room. Adjust it before dinner, not at bedtime.

slides.title: Hang the Do Not Disturb sign.
slides.body: Sleeping in? It stops an early knock from housekeeping.

slides.title: Bring a phone stand or long cable.
slides.body: Sockets are rarely next to the bed. Keep your alarm within reach.

slides.title: Book the room, then sleep well
slides.body: Compare hotels on Resapass. Link in bio.

caption:
A great hotel can still give you a bad night if you get the wrong room.

Ask for a quiet room when you book, pack earplugs and an eye mask, cool the room early and hang the Do Not Disturb sign.
